Subject: Performance Support Protocol initiation request — ethan_park (confidential)

Marissa/Markus,

I need HR and legal eyes on a proposed performance support protocol for Ethan Park (eng, IC). This is intended as a supportive, time‑boxed 60‑day plan focused on measurable outcomes and coaching cadence. Summary below and attached is my draft plan + evidence summary.

Why: Over last two quarters Ethan’s feature delivery SLA has slipped, multiple missed deadlines, and two post‑release bugs traced to incomplete QA on his work. I have documented examples in the attached evidence_summary.pdf.

What I propose (high level):
- 60 days with weekly 1:1 coaching and clear success metrics (see doc)
- Specific goals: reduce post‑release bug rate on owned modules to <1% of releases, hit assigned sprint commitments 80% of the time
- Manager checkpoints every week; mid‑point review at day 30; final evaluation at day 60
- Consequences: if progress insufficient, we escalate to formal remediation (we should align on wording and legal obligations)

Request: Please review the attached draft_support_plan_ethan_park.docx and the evidence_summary. I need:
1) Legal: any mandatory language, notice requirements, or other compliance concerns we need to include
2) HR: process checklist (meetings, documentation, who should be present), tone edits to the opening paragraph, and whether we need to loop in People Ops before manager communication

Timing: I’d like to pilot the manager conversation by end of this week if feasible. Can you review and provide comments by EOD Wed 11/11? I’m happy to hop on a 20‑minute sync to walk through specifics.

Thanks — I want to make sure we approach this supportively and defensibly.

Ben Carter
Senior Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the summary and for framing this as a supportive plan. I reviewed the draft and made edits to emphasize coaching and improvement opportunities; attached is a redline (support_plan_edits_marissa.docx). High‑level notes: 

- We should follow the standard People Ops checklist (I added the link in the doc). That includes a pre‑meeting with People Ops to confirm accommodations and to ensure consistency across similar cases.
- Tone: open with development goals and available support (mentorship, pairing time, training budget). I moved the consequence language later in the doc and softened wording to avoid sounding punitive.
- Documentation: keep weekly notes in the shared HR folder and copy People Ops on the mid‑point summary.
- Privacy: avoid internal mailing lists; limited distribution only to manager/HR/legal.

Markus, any legal flags from your side?

—Marissa
